subject: Clarifying SOC 2 coverage for Hosted / Dedicated / Private (bridge letter & evidence)
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@northstarhealth.org>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northstarhealth.org; security@northstarhealth.org
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter questions for hosting modes

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is starting the vendor review and has two quick asks before we progress to procurement:

1) Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report that covers the period Jan 1 – Dec 31 2026? If so, can you share a redacted copy and confirm whether Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private/VPC are included in that attestation or treated differently?

2) For Dedicated and Private deployments, would Redwood provide a bridge letter or attestation that maps the controls to those hosting modes (we often need a bridge when the standard SOC report primarily lists hosted endpoints)?

3) Can you list the specific evidence items we should request (audit logs, config docs, tenant isolation notes, etc.) and whether any items require an NDA / controlled access?

We attached our SIG questionnaire for reference (Northstar_SIG.xlsx). Ideally we’d like to close security review by the end of next week — is that feasible?

Best,
Elena Ramos
Senior Information Security Manager
Northstar Health

--
Attachment: Northstar_SIG.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@northstarhealth.org>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter questions for hosting modes

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the SIG. I looped in Lauren (security partnerships), Monica (solutions/eng), and Sergio (legal/compliance) so we can give a consolidated answer and hit your timeline. Quick answers up front:

- We have a SOC 2 Type II report covering 2026 (Jan 1–Dec 31). I’m attaching a redacted copy for initial review.
- Hosted API is fully covered in the report. Dedicated pools are covered when those pools are provisioned as dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity that we manage) — there are notes in the report about configuration and tenant isolation and how our sampling was done.
- Private / VPC / on-prem deployments are not always included in the standard hosted report; we typically provide a bridge letter or scoped attestation for Private deployments and can indicate which control procedures are equivalent.

Action items we’ll deliver:
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II (attached)
- A short bridge letter template that maps controls to Dedicated and Private hosting patterns
- A curated evidence checklist (audit logs, IAM config snapshots, network segmentation docs, key management notes) and guidance on items requiring an NDA or secure share

Can you confirm whether Northstar will require on-site inspection access or if Redacted/Pseudonymized artifacts over a secure link are sufficient? Also, is the SIG the source of truth or do you want us to answer the SIG directly? Happy to schedule a 30-min sync on Monday to walk through.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once the team confirms a couple of details.

— Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (redacted pdf stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai; sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II + bridge letter questions for hosting modes — internal notes

Team — forwarding Elena’s thread + my reply. Quick plan so we can respond with a single package Monday morning: 

1) Lauren — can you confirm wording we should use for Dedicated pools when they are customer-dedicated vs. multi-tenant dedicated (sampling nuance)? Recommend: "Dedicated (customer-provisioned pools) are included when the customer has a dedicated pool assignment; sampling in the 2026 report included dedicated instances where applicable." Need one crisp sentence.

2) Monica — please prepare the evidence checklist and indicate which artifacts are accessible via secure link vs. require NDA/docuSign. Include: tenant access logs, KV cache isolation docs, autoscaling config snapshots, infra network diagrams, and KMS integration notes.

3) Sergio — can you draft a bridge letter template that maps the SOC 2 control categories to our operational behaviors for Dedicated and Private, and note any controls that will need additional attestation for on-prem/private?

We should avoid saying "Private is out of scope" — instead propose bridge wording and offer to scope an addendum where needed.

I’ll assemble everything and propose a 30-min sync at 11am ET Monday. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite to Elena.

Marcus
(Internal)

Elena — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and next steps below; attaching the redacted SOC 2 and a bridge-letter template for your review.

Summary (short):
- SOC 2 Type II (2026) attached (redacted). Hosted API endpoints are explicitly covered.
- Dedicated pools: included in scope when a customer is assigned a dedicated pool; our sampling in 2026 included representative dedicated configurations. We will call out the sampling approach in the bridge letter.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: not part of the standard hosted report by default. Redwood can provide a bridge letter that maps our control families to typical Private deployment configurations and indicate any control gaps or items that would require additional evidence or a scoped attestation.

Evidence checklist (attached separate doc):
- Audit logs (runtime request/response logs, admin actions) — secure link available after NDA
- Tenant isolation & config docs (pool assignment records, tenant mapping) — secure link
- Network diagrams & segmentation (VPC peering docs for Private) — attachment or secure link
- KMS / key rotation notes (for Private we document KMS topology) — secure link
- Change management & deployment logs for Dedicated pools — secure link

What requires NDA/controlled access:
- Raw logs and tenant-specific identifiers (we can provide pseudonymized samples initially; full logs require an NDA and secure transfer).

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Northstar will accept redacted artifacts over a secure share or prefer on-site/air-gapped review.
2) If you want, we can provision a short 30-min review with our security team Monday 11am ET to walk the checklist and bridge letter.
3) If Northstar needs a signed bridge or additional attestation for Private, Sergio can draft a scoped addendum and route for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (stub); bridge_letter_template.docx (stub)

Looking forward — I’ll send the calendar invite for Monday 11am ET unless you request a different time.
